newsitem.title: USA: Marvel Holdings' old bonds extend slide, off 4 pts.
newsitem.headline: Marvel Holdings' old bonds extend slide, off 4 pts.

text.p: Debt of Marvel Holdings extended Friday's three-point drop, sliding another four points on Monday following Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's bankruptcy filing last week, traders said.
"All the focus has been on the old (Marvel Holdings') bonds ...They're the most liquid," said one high-yield trader. "They are trading at a 15 bid after going out on Friday at a 19 bid."
Others said Marvel's old bonds were seen bid as high as 16 and as low as 14-1/2 in an otherwise thin trading day.
Meanwhile, Marvel (Parent) Holdings' new bonds were bid at 11-1/2, traders added.

On Friday, Marvel Entertainment, which publishes comic books such as Spider Man and the X-Men, and its three holding companies Marvel Holdings, Marvel (Parent) Holdings and Marvel III Holdings, filed voluntary petitions for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.
In a statement, Marvel said it was forced to file because holders of the bonds issued by its holding companies failed to reach agreement on alternatives to its reorganization plan.
Since then, Marvel Holdings' (stock-backed) bonds have posted a seven-point loss in sympathy with its stock.

"The company's stock is down 3/4 from the opening. As a result, the bonds are weaker...They seem to be moving right in line with the stock," another high-yield trader said. "Old bonds were seen trading at a 15 bid."
Marvel stock, which opened down a 1/2 at 1-7/8 was off 3/4 on the day at 1-5/8 at 1507 EST/2007 GMT.
-- Nancy Leinfuss, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1675
